column1: # Known-gap ledger of hermit-cli/tests/deadline_slice_cap.rs on KVM. ci/kvm-gap-ledger.rs reads it
# for the validation node privileged-test.deadline_slice_cap_kvm, which runs the whole suite on
# --backend=kvm and names this file in its environment (HERMIT_KNOWN_GAP_LEDGER). The format is
# documented in ci/manifest-plan/src/known_gaps.rs; the receipt qualifier and the scorecard read it.
# Every test of the suite that is NOT listed here must pass on KVM, so a new test is required on
# KVM by default. A listed test is a known gap. The node still runs it, and it must fail exactly as
# its row says: an ordinary failure whose output contains the signature, or a stop by the per-test
# CPU budget. That failure is a non-blocking diagnostic failure (KNOWN-KVM-GAP), never a pass. A
# listed test that passes, or fails some other way, fails the node. When a gap is fixed, delete its
# row, raise the node's pinned count (privileged-test.deadline_slice_cap_kvm in
# NEXTEST_EXPECTED_COUNTS), and run ./ci/sync-cell-config.sh to refresh the scorecard.
# A signature is text the failure's output must show; in it \n is a newline, \\ a backslash and
# <N> any run of digits.
# The ledger can only shrink; `make lint-checks` (lint-check-known-gap-ledgers) holds it to its
# history. "baseline" marks a row present, unchanged, since the ledger was introduced, with the
# coordinator's approval of 2026-10-30. A row added later, or one whose outcome or signature
# changes, carries the full URL of a specific approving comment, review or commit in its approval
# field, and its commit message binds that URL to the row with a line
#     KVM-Gap-Approval: <URL> <id>
# A required test that leaves the suite or is #[ignore]d needs the same with KVM-Required-Removal.
# The check reads first parents only: put approval lines on commits that land by rebase, not on a
# merged side branch. Run `make lint-check-known-gap-ledgers` before landing any change to this
# file or to the suite (validation runs it in check.lint_checks): a version the check cannot read
# blocks it until the checker itself changes.
# Gaps: T2 = KVM's preemption timer is off, so KVM refuses --max-timeslice before the guest
# starts, or never preempts a spinner; T2+oracle = the same, and the test's oracle also reads a
# reverie-ptrace log line; C, D, E, E+F' and G = the gaps of that letter in
# https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4929.
